title: Parameter estimation and identifiability analysis for a bivalent analyte model of monoclonal antibody-antigen binding
authors: Kyle Nguyen; Kan Li; Kevin Flores; Georgia D. Tomaras; S. Moses Dennison; Janice M. McCarthy
one_liner_zh: 该文研究抗体-抗原双价结合动力学参数估计与可辨识性分析，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作建模，但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且方法为ODE拟合与统计辨识，无AI或MD等本课题核心方法，仅部分启发可迁移。
abstract: 1 Abstract Discovery research for therapeutic antibodies and vaccine development requires an in-depth understanding of antibody-antigen interactions. Label-free techniques such as Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) enable the characterization of biomolecular interactions through kinetics measurements, typically by binding antigens in solution to monoclonal antibodies immobilized on a SPR chip. 1:1 Langmuir binding model is commonly used to fit the kinetics data and derive rate constants. However, in certain contexts it is necessary to immobilize the antigen to the chip and flow the antibodies in solution. One such scenario is the screening of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) for breadth against a range of antigens, where a bivalent analyte binding model is required to adequately describe the kinetics data unless antigen immobilizaion density is optimized to eliminate avidity effects. A bivalent analyte model is offered in several existing software packages intended for standard throughput SPR instruments, but lacking for high throughput SPR instruments. Existing methods also do not explore multiple local minima and parameter identifiability, issues common in non-linear optimization. Here, we have developed a method for analyzing bivalent analyte binding kinetics directly applicable to high throughput SPR data collected in a non-regenerative fashion, and have included a grid search on initial parameter values and a profile likelihood method to determine parameter identifiability. We fit the data of a broadly neutralizing HIV-1 mAb binding to HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein gp120 to a system of ordinary differential equations modeling bivalent binding. Our identifiability analysis discovered a non-identifiable parameter when data is collected under the standard experimental design for monitoring the association and dissociation phases. We used simulations to determine an improved experimental design, which when executed, resulted in the reliable estimation of all rate constants. These methods will be valuable tools in analyzing the binding of mAbs to an array of antigens to expedite therapeutic antibody discovery research. 2 Author summary While commercial software programs for the analysis of bivalent analyte binding kinetics are available for low-throughput instruments, they cannot be easily applied to data generated by high-throughput instruments, particularly when the chip surface is not regenerated between titration cycles. Further, existing software does not address common issues in fitting non-linear systems of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) such as optimizations getting trapped in local minima or parameters that are not identifiable. In this work, we introduce a pipeline for analysis of bivalent analyte binding kinetics that 1) allows for the use of high-throughput, non-regenerative experimental designs, 2) optimizes using several sets of initial parameter values to ensure that the algorithm is able to reach the lowest minimum error and 3) applies a profile likelihood method to explore parameter identifiability. In our experimental application of the method, we found that one of the kinetics parameters ( k d 2 ) cannot be reliably estimated with the standard length of the dissociation phase. Using simulation and identifiability analysis we determined the optimal length of dissociation so that the parameter can be reliably estimated, saving time and reagents. These methodologies offer robust determination of the kinetics parameters for high-throughput bivalent analyte SPR experiments.
abstract_zh:
1 摘要 治疗性抗体和疫苗开发中的发现研究需要深入了解抗体-抗原相互作用。无标记技术，如表面等离子体共振 (Surface Plasmon Resonance, SPR)，能够通过动力学测量表征生物分子相互作用，通常是将溶液中的抗原结合到固定在SPR芯片上的单克隆抗体上。1:1 Langmuir结合模型通常用于拟合动力学数据并推导速率常数。然而，在某些情况下，有必要将抗原固定在芯片上，并使抗体在溶液中流动。一种此类场景是针对一系列抗原筛选单克隆抗体 (monoclonal antibodies, mAbs) 的广度，此时需要二价分析物结合模型来充分描述动力学数据，除非抗原固定密度经过优化以消除亲合力效应。现有几种软件包中提供了二价分析物模型，适用于标准通量SPR仪器，但缺乏针对高通量SPR仪器的支持。现有方法也未探索多个局部最小值和参数可识别性，这些是非线性优化中的常见问题。在此，我们开发了一种直接适用于以非再生方式收集的高通量SPR数据的二价分析物结合动力学分析方法，并包含了初始参数值的网格搜索和轮廓似然方法以确定参数可识别性。我们将广泛中和HIV-1 mAb与HIV-1包膜糖蛋白gp120结合的数据拟合到建模二价结合的常微分方程组中。我们的可识别性分析发现，在监测结合和解离阶段的标准实验设计下收集数据时，存在一个不可识别参数。我们使用模拟确定了一种改进的实验设计，执行该设计后，所有速率常数均能可靠估计。这些方法将成为分析mAb与一系列抗原结合以加速治疗性抗体发现研究的有价值工具。

2 作者总结 虽然用于二价分析物结合动力学分析的商业软件程序可用于低通量仪器，但它们难以轻易应用于高通量仪器生成的数据，特别是在滴定循环之间不再生芯片表面的情况下。此外，现有软件未解决拟合非线性常微分方程组 (ODEs) 中的常见问题，如优化陷入局部最小值或参数不可识别。在本工作中，我们引入了一个用于二价分析物结合动力学分析的流程，该流程1) 允许使用高通量、非再生实验设计，2) 使用多组初始参数值进行优化，以确保算法能够达到最低最小误差，3) 应用轮廓似然方法探索参数可识别性。在我们对该方法的实验应用中，我们发现其中一个动力学参数 ( k d 2 ) 在标准长度的解离阶段下无法可靠估计。通过模拟和可识别性分析，我们确定了最佳解离长度，以便该参数能够可靠估计，从而节省时间和试剂。这些方法为高通量二价分析物SPR实验提供了动力学参数的稳健确定。
